children: ) is preparing to raise prices on parts of its snack and beverage portfolio after earlier cuts failed to produce a meaningful sales rebound, highlighting the difficult trade-off between protecting affordability and restoring margins. The planned increases suggest PepsiCo sees limited benefit from keeping prices aggressively low when North American food volumes remain flat and costs continue rising.
The increases are expected to hit grocery-store-sized bags of Doritos, Ruffles and SunChips late this year or in early 2027, with some chip prices rising by a low- to mid-single-digit percentage.

The move comes only months after PepsiCo cut prices on several major chip brands by as much as 15% in February. The reductions were designed to revive demand after some products had climbed above $7 per bag.
So far, the response has been underwhelming.

PepsiCo's North American food business reported a 2% revenue decline in its most recent quarter, while volumes were flat. That suggests lower prices were not enough to materially improve demand, leaving the company with weaker revenue and continued cost pressure.
PepsiCo has already increased prices on some larger Tostitos salsa jars and Fritos canned dips, while some soft-drink prices are also expected to rise.

The company told Bloomberg that prices after the new increases would still remain below levels seen before the earlier reductions, indicating PepsiCo is trying to reclaim some pricing power without fully abandoning its affordability strategy.
For PepsiCo investors, the key issue is whether modest price increases can improve revenue and margins without pushing already-stretched consumers away.
Investors should watch North American food volumes, organic revenue growth, gross margin and promotional activity.

If volumes remain stable even as prices rise, PepsiCo could regain some earnings leverage after its earlier affordability push. But if consumers respond by buying less, the company may end up back in the same demand problem it was trying to solve.
The coming quarters will show whether PepsiCo has found a better balance between price, volume and profitability.

title: PepsiCo Makes Surprising U-Turn on Snack Prices
